CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain with right leg tingling

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports that while raking leaves in his yard yesterday, he felt fine. Approximately two hours after coming inside, he developed back tightening and experienced pins and needles sensation in his right leg. He has had a similar episode of back pain approximately three years ago which resolved after one day. He tried ice and two tablets of ibuprofen (Advil) without relief. A hot shower provided some relief, and his pain improves when sitting. On examination, he reports pain with forward bending but no pain with standing/extension. He experiences pain with palpation around the L5 region. He also reports tingling sensation in his right leg.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Low back pain approximately three years ago that resolved spontaneously.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (Advil) - recently attempted, 2 tablets, without relief.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Raking leaves in yard yesterday. Patient normally does not do much physical activity.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Back: Palpation of L5 region elicits pain. Range of motion: Pain with forward bending; no pain with standing/extension. Neurological: Dorsiflexion strength normal. Pulses equal in all extremities. Tingling sensation noted in right leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of low back: normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Low back strain/sprain. Recommended rest. Meloxicam prescribed. Physical therapy referral for flexibility and strengthening exercises given patient's sedentary lifestyle. Follow-up via phone call in 2 weeks. If symptoms do not improve, will obtain MRI to evaluate for additional pathology.
